screening.reason: Inclusion 2-3: a secondary/validation cohort drawn from ABIDE rs-fMRI data is analysed for thalamocortical group-difference (ASD vs TD) connectivity.

evidence_spans.text:
The secondary cohort was a subset of the ABIDE database
consisting of 58 HFASD (25.4[7.8] years, 37.9% female) and 51 typically developing controls (24.4[6.7] years, 39.2%
female).
evidence_spans.claim: The secondary (ABIDE) cohort consisted of 58 high-functioning ASD and 51 typically developing controls.

evidence_spans.text:
To validate our ﬁndings in a separate cohort, we iden-
tiﬁed 58 ASD and 51 TD individuals from ABIDE mat-
ched to the HFASD cohort by age, sex, and IQ (Table 2).
The selection process is detailed in Supplemental Infor-
mation.
evidence_spans.claim: 58 ASD and 51 TD individuals were identified from ABIDE, matched to the primary HFASD cohort by age, sex and IQ.

evidence_spans.text:
Func-
tional data from both the HFASD and ABIDE cohorts
were preprocessed identically using fMRIPrep v1.3.152, a
pipeline that uses a combination of tools from existing
neuroimaging software packages.
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE (and HFASD) functional data were preprocessed identically using the fMRIPrep v1.3.1 pipeline.

evidence_spans.text:
In the ABIDE cohort, group-mean FD was
0.124 for ASD and 0.123 for TD (two sample t-test p =
0.8679).
evidence_spans.claim: Group-mean framewise displacement in the ABIDE cohort was 0.124 (ASD) and 0.123 (TD), not significantly different.

evidence_spans.text:
Frames that exhibited an FD of over 0.5 mm were
censored from the timeseries, as well as one before and
two after the offending frame.
evidence_spans.claim: Frames with FD over 0.5 mm (plus one before and two after) were censored (scrubbed) from the timeseries.

evidence_spans.text:
Participants with <80% of
their TRs retained after motion scrubbing were removed
from the analysis. As a result, a total of 20 TD participants
and 23 ASD participants were analyzed from the HFASD
cohort (Table 1). From ABIDE, 51 TD participants and 58
ASD participants were analyzed (Table 2).
evidence_spans.claim: Participants retaining under 80% of TRs after motion scrubbing were excluded, leaving 51 TD and 58 ASD from ABIDE.

evidence_spans.text:
To account for potential con-
founding effects from differences in scan acquisition
parameters, we included site as a covariate in our ABIDE
GLM analysis as one-hot encoded variables.
evidence_spans.claim: Site was included as a one-hot-encoded covariate in the ABIDE GLM analysis to account for differences in scan acquisition parameters.

evidence_spans.text:
In the ABIDE GLM analysis, clusters were found that
had greater connectivity with the right thalamus in the
ASD group compared to the TD group. Two of these
clusters were located in the right precentral (p = 0.019)
and postcentral gyri (p = 0.028), validating the observed
hyperconnectivity of the same regions in our HFASD
cohort.
evidence_spans.claim: In the ABIDE validation analysis, right thalamus connectivity with right precentral (p=0.019) and postcentral gyri (p=0.028) was greater in ASD than TD, replicating the primary-cohort finding.

assessments.support: ABIDE subset selection is matched by age, sex and IQ, but the full selection process is deferred to Supplemental Information not present in the extracted full text.
ABIDE demographics (N, age, sex, FSIQ) are tabulated (Table 2) with between-group p-values.
ABIDE data preprocessed identically to the primary cohort with fMRIPrep v1.3.1, with explicit FD-based scrubbing and retention thresholds.
Diagnosis source for the ABIDE subset specifically (vs. the primary HFASD cohort's ADI-R/ADOS confirmation) is not restated in the main text.
Age, sex, IQ matching and motion (FD) are reported and compared between groups; site is explicitly modeled.
Site included as one-hot-encoded covariate in the ABIDE GLM; motion handled via scrubbing and a TR-retention threshold.
Seed-based whole-brain GLM connectivity analysis with the same five a priori seeds as the primary cohort.
Bonferroni correction for five seeds (p=0.01 cluster threshold) is explicitly applied.

risk_of_bias.summary: ABIDE validation cohort is matched and preprocessed identically to the primary cohort with documented motion QC, site covariate handling, and multiple-comparisons correction; main uncertainty is that exact ABIDE inclusion/exclusion selection is deferred to an unretrieved supplement.

charting.title: Thalamocortical connectivity is associated with autism symptoms in high-functioning adults with autism and typically developing adults
charting.primary_goal: Validate thalamocortical hyperconnectivity findings from a primary HFASD cohort in an independent ABIDE-derived cohort
charting.specific_features: Whole-thalamus seed-based connectivity (5 seeds: left/right thalamus and others) to whole-brain voxelwise GLM
charting.feature_change_direction: Hyperconnectivity (ASD > TD) between right thalamus and right precentral/postcentral gyri in the ABIDE validation cohort
charting.summary_key_findings: In an independent ABIDE-derived cohort (58 ASD, 51 TD) matched for age, sex and IQ, right thalamus hyperconnectivity with right precentral and postcentral gyri in ASD vs TD replicated the primary HFASD cohort's finding (p=0.019 and p=0.028 respectively, after site-covariate adjustment and Bonferroni correction).
charting.features_associated_disorder: Right thalamus to right precentral gyrus and right postcentral gyrus hyperconnectivity in ASD vs TD
charting.reviewer_notes: ABIDE is used only as a secondary/validation cohort; the primary cohort (23 ASD, 20 TD) is the lab's own non-ABIDE sample.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) seed-based connectivity study; primary cohort is the authors' own lab sample (23 ASD, 20 TD); ABIDE-derived secondary/validation cohort: 58 ASD, 51 TD, matched by age/sex/IQ.
narrative_row.methods: Both cohorts preprocessed identically with fMRIPrep v1.3.1; FD-based scrubbing (>0.5mm) and <80% TR-retention exclusion; whole-thalamus seed-based whole-brain GLM connectivity with site as a covariate in the ABIDE analysis; Bonferroni correction for five seeds.
narrative_row.outcomes: Right thalamus hyperconnectivity with right precentral/postcentral gyri in ASD vs TD replicated in the ABIDE cohort (p=0.019, p=0.028), supporting thalamocortical hyperconnectivity in high-functioning adult ASD.
narrative_row.key_limitations: ABIDE selection process detailed only in an unretrieved supplement; diagnosis source for ABIDE subset not independently restated; whole-thalamus (not nuclei-specific) seeds used due to low-resolution imaging.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates use of ABIDE as an independent validation cohort for an associational finding originating in a non-ABIDE sample, with explicit site-covariate handling and motion QC thresholds applied to the ABIDE subset.

kg_link.finding: Right thalamus connectivity with right precentral gyrus (p=0.019) and right postcentral gyrus (p=0.028) was greater in ASD than TD in the ABIDE cohort, replicating hyperconnectivity found in an independent primary HFASD cohort.
